from_notes: Word length | Bits the CPU handles at once (32-bit, 64-bit)
x: Word length is the number of bits the CPU handles at once (32-bit, 64-bit), so it is measured in bits; a byte is a fixed group of 8 bits, not the unit of word length.

from_notes: Clock speed of a processor is measured in hertz – gigahertz (GHz)
x: GHz (gigahertz, a billion cycles per second) measures the clock speed of the processor; pixels and resolution describe displays and storage is measured in bytes.
Tianhe-1A (2010) was built by China's National University of Defense Technology (NUDT) and topped the TOP500 list in Nov 2010; Japan is the tempting wrong option.
Parallel computing splits a large problem into smaller parts that are solved at the same time on several processors; the 'anti-' and 'socialised' options are not computing terms.
source: general knowledge (standard definition, e.g. Britannica 'parallel processing'); notes only list parallel processing under the fifth generation [3:1.4]

x: Bandwidth, the data-transfer rate in bits per second, is the printed key and a standard performance measure; lanwidth and comwidth are not real terms.
source: printed key, not verified; row-12 notes (runs/b5-r012/notes/row-12.md) sub 4 [4:9.2]; web search: bandwidth listed among computer-performance metrics (cseweb.ucsd.edu CSE240A performance lecture)
evidence: web search: no source for the exact APPSC 2004 question; bandwidth appears in performance-metric lists, 'datawidth' does not
dispute: Printed key: Bandwidth. Strictly, data width (word length, the bits a CPU handles at once) is also a measure of a computer's power.

x: 1 byte = 8 bits, so 1024 bits ÷ 8 = 128 bytes; 1 MB is 1024 × 1024 bytes, far larger.
In a multiple-choice question the answer is shown and must only be recognised among options, so it uses recognition; recall (as in essay or fill-in questions) means retrieving it without cues.
source: general psychology (recognition vs recall, e.g. Britannica 'memory: recognition'); printed key agrees

x: A web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) is application software that fetches webpages from the web and displays them on the screen; a search engine only finds pages.
Ctrl + X is Cut: it copies the selection to the clipboard (memory) and removes it from the document; Ctrl + C only copies and Ctrl + Z undoes.
source: Microsoft Support 'Keyboard shortcuts in Word' (support.microsoft.com); cut/copy/paste: Larry Tesler, notes [3:7.6]

from_notes: Clock speed ... GHz; translators = system software; MS Word = application software
x: CPU speed is in hertz, RAM size in bytes, a compiler is system software and MS Word is application software, so A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3; baud is a signalling rate for data transmission.

from_notes: 2GL assembly | Mnemonics; converted by an assembler (not a compiler)
x: Assembly language (2GL mnemonics) is converted into machine code by an assembler, not by a compiler; the other options are not translators.
The mode is the value that occurs most often (maximum frequency); the mean is the average and the median the middle value.
source: general statistics (mode definition, NCERT Class 11 Statistics for Economics ch.5); printed key agrees
